name: Mils
kurzbeschreibung: A quiet yet centrally located market town on the left bank of the Inn, featuring a castle and the Baroque church of St. Peter.
text:
Overview

Mils bei Hall is situated in the Tyrolean Unterinntal on a sunny terrace at 605 meters above sea level, located immediately east of the historic salt town of Hall in Tirol and just twelve kilometers east of Innsbruck. The municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district has around 4,600 residents and stretches from the fertile plains of the Inn River up into the forested southern foothills of the Karwendel mountains. Due to its protected, sun-drenched plateau position, Mils benefits from an exceptionally mild microclimate, earning it a long-standing reputation as a pleasant summer retreat and coveted residential community. Despite modern residential growth, Mils retains its proud village traditions, generous recreational green belts, and panoramic vistas across to the Tux Alps.

History

Thanks to its favorable climate, settlement in Mils dates back to Roman times, as proved by coins and burial sites found in the area. The earliest official record appeared between 930 and 940 AD under the name 'Milles', a Celtic-Romanic toponym referring to a mill or gravel alluvial soil. During the High Middle Ages, local history was closely intertwined with the noble Knights of Mils. Knight Oswald Milser gained legendary infamy through the miraculous Host incident at Seefeld in 1384; his ornately sculpted Gothic tomb slab can still be admired inside the parish church. The parish church of the Assumption (Mariä Himmelfahrt) preserves late Gothic foundations but was nearly destroyed in a catastrophic village fire in 1791. It was rebuilt in an elegant late Baroque and classicist design, later adorned with vibrant ceiling frescoes by celebrated Tyrolean painter Franz Plattner.

Getting There

Reaching Mils is quick and convenient due to first-rate transport infrastructure in the Innsbruck metropolitan corridor. Motorists travel along the A12 Inntal Autobahn, taking exit Hall-Mitte or Hall-Ost, reaching the village center via connecting roads in just three minutes. By rail, passengers travel to Hall in Tirol station, a major stop on the Tyrolean S-Bahn network served frequently from Innsbruck, Jenbach, and Kufstein. From Hall station and Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, regional bus lines 505 and 4134 run at frequent 15- to 30-minute intervals directly to Mils. Cyclists can also reach the village conveniently along the Inn River Cycle Path (Inn-Radweg).

Tips

Mils provides an ideal starting point for peaceful walks and nature excursions. A particular highlight is the Mils–Gnadenwald Path of Contemplation (Besinnungsweg), which winds through tranquil meadows and forest edges beneath the Karwendel ridge, featuring meditative artistic waypoints. Nature lovers will enjoy the protected Milser Heide heath and the serene Milser Auen riparian woodlands along the river, which harbor diverse bird species. Cultural enthusiasts should visit the parish church to view Oswald Milser's historic grave monument and explore historic manors such as Schloss Grasegg. With the medieval center of Hall in Tirol and Swarovski Crystal Worlds in Wattens just minutes away, Mils blends cultural discovery with gentle outdoor recreation.
